**Finding: COMPLIANT (sits at/above the LOL-CAP fallback; no redline proposed).**

Locations inspected: Section 6.2(a) (p0283), Section 6.2(b)/(d) (p0284, p0286), Section 5.2 (p0242–p0245), Section 6.3 indemnities (p0290–p0299), Section 9.6 limited recourse (p0378), Section 9.7 (p0380–p0382), arbitration damages bar (p0469), Indenture Trustee cost carve-out (p0454). Targeted searches for "exceed", "consequential", "waived and released", "confidential" and "liability" confirm no aggregate cap, no fee-based ceiling and no "shall not exceed" formula anywhere in the document.

Why compliant:
- **Mutual and symmetric.** Section 6.2(a) and Section 5.2(a) apply identical "specific obligations only / liable only for willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence" language to Cellco and to the Depositor respectively.
- **Nothing is capped, so the fallback carve-outs are satisfied a fortiori.** Cellco's Section 6.3 indemnity to the Issuer and trustees for willful misconduct, bad faith and gross negligence is uncapped in amount.
- **Direction check.** Adding a mutual 12-months-of-fees cap would newly cap Cellco's currently uncapped indemnity against a Servicing Fee base — a material weakening of our position — so we do not redline to reach the preferred wording.
- **Our exposure is separately protected.** Section 9.6 confines any claim against the Depositor or Issuer to the Depositor Transferred Property, a one-sided limit in our favour with no counterpart for Cellco. No walk-away trigger is present.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged (preferred-only refinements with no adverse effect absent a cap): no free-standing mutual consequential-damages exclusion (p0469 binds only the arbitral panel), no USD 1,000,000 floor, no express confidentiality/data-protection or IP super-carve-outs, and no payment-obligations exclusion.
